summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality regression checks and prompt tuning. Reviewed latest scoring, discussed a small regression on long-context summarization after quantization, agreed on guardrail tuning and follow-up benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alyssa Morgan (Redwood AE), Jason Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Orchid Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Eng Manager), Tara Nguyen (Product), Devon (intern)
Shared: prompt-set-v2.csv (link), scoring-dashboard (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/ORCH-POC), guardrails draft (drive link)

00:00 - Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check on audio - can you hear me?
00:05 - Priya: Yeah thanks, can hear you fine. Sorry slight delay i just stepped out of a standup.
00:12 - Jason: Awesome. so agenda today: quick status, go through latest quality numbers, talk about the one regression we saw on long context summarization after we applied 4-bit quant, and then next steps.
01:02 - Marco: sounds good. we ran the new prompt set overnight and pushed results into your scoring sheet, there are a couple of weird outliers.
01:18 - Alyssa: Great — we'll pull that up. Jason, do you want to start with the scoring dashboard?
01:25 - Jason: yeah, pulling it up now. so high level: overall pass rate is stable at ~82% on our core 300 prompts, embeddings similarity unchanged, but on the 200 long-context summarization prompts we saw average ROUGE-L drop from 0.72 to 0.61 after v2 quantization, that's the main regression.
02:05 - Priya: hmm ok that's a bit bigger than we expected. can you remind us what changed between v1 and v2?
02:12 - Jason: sure — v2 switches to 4-bit dynamic quant plus new pruning for attention heads that were dormant in pretraining. That reduced memory and cost by ~30% in our bench, but it looks like some long-range attention behaviour degraded.
02:30 - Tara: i want to flag this is customer-visible, our summarization flows must keep key facts intact; false negatives there -> product risk.
02:40 - Alyssa: yeah agreed. two paths: we can tweak the quant profile (less aggressive on certain layers), or we can add guardrail heuristics to detect low-confidence summaries and fallback to the non-quantized variant.
03:05 - Priya: fallback makes sense but cost is a concern if it happens often. what's the false positive rate on the guardrails?
03:12 - Jason: currently prototype guardrails flag around 6% of summaries; of those ~40% are true failures and 60% are false positives — so we need to tighten thresholds.
03:28 - Marco: can you show an example of a false positive?
03:34 - Jason: sure reading from the spreadsheet — prompt ID 241, original target mentions three entities, quantized model returned the entities but reordered one and paraphrased an amount; the guardrail flagged because entity overlap score slipped below 0.8 threshold. It actually was acceptable for this use case, so threshold too strict.
04:08 - Priya: ok so we tune threshold up, and also add a weighted metric that prioritizes numeric stability for financial UIs.
04:22 - Jason: yep we can add a composite score: entity overlap weighted 0.6, numeric exactness 0.3, fluency 0.1 — threshold tuned per workflow.
05:00 - Alyssa: good. next, quality eval: we also ran a small human eval of 50 samples. Priya and Tara, thanks for the annotations. human pass rate aligned with automated score about 85% for non-long-context, but for the long-context human pass rate dipped to 68%.
05:35 - Priya: those human labels show that the model sometimes hallucinated a historical sequence; it was subtle.
05:42 - Devon: one thing i noticed is that the tokenizer splits currency expressions inconsistently which may affect numeric matching.
05:48 - Jason: good catch, tokenizer mismatch was not re-tested post-quant. we'll add a tokenization normalization step in pre-processing for the scoring pipeline.
06:10 - Marco: are we seeing latency regressions with quant? i thought quant reduces latency but might increase CPU overhead for decoding.
06:20 - Jason: in our infra bench, quantization decreased GPU memory and increased throughput slightly but tail latency on long-context increased by ~10% due to extra CPU-based postprocessing for KV cache alignment. We're going to try a kernel change in the runtime to move that onto GPU.
07:00 - Priya: ok timeline — how fast can you run the 1,000-prompt regression with tuned quant profile?
07:06 - Jason: we can re-run overnight if we lock the tuned config today, deliver CSV and delta charts by Wednesday 2025-08-06.
07:18 - Alyssa: we'll target that. on guardrails, we propose two-tier approach: 1) relax threshold for non-critical fields, 2) mandatory fallback when numeric/exactness metrics fail.
07:35 - Tara: for product, we want a configurable knob in the console to set fallback policy per route. does Redwood Console support per-route policies in the POC?
07:44 - Jason: yes, the current POC config exposes per-route policies; we can demo in the console next session. it's behind a feature flag but available.
08:06 - Priya: another ask, can you include a small sample of the false positive logs so we can triage quickly?
08:12 - Alyssa: yes will include sample rows and the raw model outputs. we'll redact PII.
08:18 - Marco: on evaluation metrics, can you add a column for "semantic correctness" that we can use in UI prioritization?
08:25 - Jason: yes, semantic correctness will be an additional derived metric — we'll add to scoring sheet and re-score the 300 core prompts.
08:48 - Priya: question about security — we need to verify logs and audit trail for any fallback to non-quantized model (for compliance). do you log decisions and payloads?
08:58 - Jason: yes, decision logs are captured in the control plane with request id, policy reason, and model variant; payloads are redacted by default but can be sent to a private S3 when customer opts in.
09:12 - Priya: perfect. would need SOC2 doc and SSO checklist for our security team.
09:20 - Alyssa: i'll send SOC2 summary and the SSO checklist today.
09:24 - Tara: also, pricing note — if fallback usage is >10% we need a cost cap or alerting.
09:31 - Alyssa: noted — we'll include a cost-guard in the Console and alerting rule sample.
09:38 - Marco: regarding competitor comparison, we've been testing OpenAI and Anthropic in parallel; at similar cost point we saw slightly different hallucination patterns, but Redwood's runtime makes the quantization/cost tradeoffs easier to tweak.
09:55 - Jason: small note: for the dedicated benchmark run, we should provision 2x capacity for burst to mimic your peak. Alyssa can share pricing for that.
10:10 - Alyssa: will do. alright, quick demo point: Jason, can you run through the one counterexample where quantized output failed and show the guardrail trace?
10:18 - Jason: yep — jumping to prompt 241, here's raw output... (reads aloud) 
10:40 - Jason: guardrail trace shows entity score 0.72, numeric exactness 0.62, composite 0.68 (threshold 0.75) so flagged. if threshold lowered to 0.65 this would pass; however it still has minor reorder, product may accept that.
11:05 - Priya: for finance summaries reorder is serious sometimes, so i'd rather fallback than accept lower threshold for those routes.
11:12 - Jason: ok we'll mark route "finance-summaries" as strict by default.
11:20 - Tara: one more product ask: can fallback be rate-limited so we don't exceed budget?
11:27 - Jason: yes we support quota-based fallback with percentage cap per route. we'll sample and send a suggested default of 5% with alerting.
11:40 - Alyssa: wrap up recap: Jason will run 1k regression on tuned quant profile and add semantic correctness & token normalization; Priya will validate guardrail FP logs; Alyssa will send SOC2 and pricing. we'll reconvene next Wednesday same time.
11:58 - Priya: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turn.
12:03 - Alyssa: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription has small mislabels and occasional filler words removed for readability. Raw recording available on request.
